subject: NovaSynth joint validation workshop & reference architecture

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: NovaSynth Partnerships <partnerships@novasynth.co>, Eleanor Park <eleanor@novasynth.co>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: NovaSynth — joint technical validation workshop proposal

Hi Eleanor / NovaSynth team,

Thanks again for the productive sync last week. As discussed, we should run a focused technical validation workshop to:
- validate integration points for NovaSynth's inference path (input batching, cache hints)
- agree on a reference architecture for embedding Redwood's runtime into your deployment model
- exercise a short end-to-end smoke test on a sample workload

Proposed slots:
- Tue May 18 (10:00–13:00 PT) — hands-on lab + architecture review
- Wed May 19 (13:00–16:00 PT) — performance tuning and SLA mapping

Ask: please share a short product diagram and the current onboarding/runbook you use for partner integrations. I attached a lightweight runbook template to speed alignment.

I'll coordinate internal pre-reads and bring a sandbox image + example workload. Sergio, can you lead the sandbox prep? Karthik, can you draft the quantization/serving notes for discussion?

Attachments: runbook-template.xlsx (stub)

Thanks,
Michael

Thanks Michael — this looks good. May 18/19 both work for us; we prefer May 18 for the hands-on portion and May 19 for tuning, as you suggested.

Looping in Rajiv (tech lead) — he will join for the architecture and performance sessions. I've attached a short product overview and our current integration checklist so you have context.

Notes from our side:
- Our deployment model supports both hosted and on-prem runtime; for the trial we'll spin up a staging cluster in our AWS account.
- Primary constraints: max request sizes, and we do short-lived pods with aggressive auto-scaling.

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: NovaSynth — joint technical validation workshop proposal

Sergio / Karthik — forwarding NovaSynth confirmation and a couple quick asks to get us ready:

1) Sergio: please provision the sandbox image (small vCPU/GPU pool) in our staging tenant and prepare the smoke dataset (500–1k short prompts). Plan: we will mirror their short-lived pod behavior (aggressive autoscaling) and validate cache behavior under churn.

2) Karthik: put together a two-page note covering: recommended quantization profile (4-bit/8-bit tradeoffs), batching policy for sub-100ms p95 SLO, and fallback routing for reduced capacity. Keep it practical — we'll review in the pre-read.

3) Everyone: I'll draft a 90-minute hands-on agenda and share a reference architecture PDF (initial draft) by tomorrow. Eleanor/Rajiv — if you can confirm their preferred auth/KMS approach ahead of the workshop that will help (they mentioned KMS options in the product diagram).

Quoted for context:
> From: Eleanor Park <eleanor@novasynth.co>
> Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: NovaSynth — joint technical validation workshop proposal

Thanks — target is to have the pre-read pack and infra up by Friday. Sergio, Karthik — if either of you foresee any blockers, flag them here and we'll escalate.

Michael
Partner Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 08:00:00 -0700
Subject: NovaSynth technical validation — agenda, calendar invite, and reference arch (v0)

Hi all — sending the confirmed invite for May 18 (10:00–13:00 PT) and May 19 (13:00–16:00 PT). Agenda attached along with a first-pass reference architecture PDF.

Quick highlights:
- Day 1 (Hands-on): environment smoke test, prefix/KV cache validation, latency profiling across 1–4 concurrent workers.
- Day 2 (Tuning): quantization experiments, batching policy tradeoffs, routing & fallback tests.
- Success criteria: reproducible p95 <= 150ms on the sample workload; deterministic KV cache hit rate > 70% for prefix-heavy flows.

Attachments: novasynth-tech-validation-agenda.pdf (stub), reference-arch-draft.pdf (stub)

Please accept the calendar invite. Sergio — we need the sandbox image and dataset by end of day Friday. Karthik — I'll slot 30 minutes in the pre-read review to run through your notes.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to it.

Michael Grant
